visual_text: Low-intake dehydration, people aged 65 and over
Reference test, screen, and a sign to watch
Serum osmolality (295 mOsm/kg or more: starting or present)
Missed drinks between meals: promising in one study of 71
A screen, not a diagnosis. Best of 39 formulas in 595 older people.
All in mmol/L. Result in mOsm/L.
At 295 mOsm/L or more: picks up about 85 in 100 dehydrated people; flags about 41 in 100 who are not
Hooper et al., BMJ Open 2015; Siervo et al., Am J Clin Nutr 2014
alt_text: Card 1 of 2. Single bedside signs are not useful alone for low-intake dehydration in people 65 and over: urine colour, urine specific gravity, dry mouth, thirst, heart rate, recorded fluid intake. Alongside: serum osmolality as reference test, calculated osmolarity as a screen, and missed drinks between meals as a promising sign.

Card 2 of 2. Calculated osmolarity equals 1.86 times (sodium plus potassium) plus 1.15 times glucose plus urea plus 14, all in mmol/L. At 295 mOsm/L or more it flags about 85 in 100 dehydrated people and 41 in 100 who are not, shown as two icon arrays. A screen, not a diagnosis.
design_instructions: Carousel 2 cards. Card 1 two-column comparison (not useful alone vs reference test, screen, sign). Card 2 equation on mint panel with terms in different tones, two 10x10 icon arrays (85 teal, 41 orange) with captions. Claim C13-20-e.
